transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Monday, October 12. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Delhi Metro shuts 6 stations till 4pm amid Congress march; traffic curbs likely. Entry and exit at six Delhi Metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat and Patel Chowk, will remain closed from 6 am to 4 pm on Monday due to security concerns amid Congress' call for a protest march to the Supreme Court, while interchange facilities will continue to be available at the affected stations, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said. CJP raises 'phone hacking' doubts, to continue protest. Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das from Cockroach Janata Party addressed journalists regarding their recent detention. They expressed fears about potential phone hacking after being separated from their devices by police. The activists emphasized their commitment to protesting until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns and accountability is established. Allegations of police misconduct, including the assault of protesters and detaining of student leaders, were also raised. Delhi-NCR wakes up to heavy rain, thunderstorms. Delhi experienced heavy rain and thunderstorms on Monday morning, leading to a noticeable change in weather. The India Meteorological Department predicted moderate to heavy rainfall for the next few hours. While cooler temperatures prevail, maximum temperatures are expected to range between 31 and 35 degrees Celsius. The IMD also forecasted partly cloudy skies and no rainfall over the next six days. Couple rejects $131,000 offer for data center power line on their property. Jerry Zelenka has turned down American Transmission Company's proposal to place a power line on his property, citing worries over tree removal and the demolition of numerous buildings. He is particularly troubled by the level of compensation offered and the potential threat of eminent domain. Meanwhile, legal disputes from neighboring landowners about the project's validity persist. 'Let them do whatever': Shami breaks silence on continued India snubs. Mohammed Shami has been out of favour with the national selectors, but he said he would continue playing wherever he gets an opportunity instead of worrying about his return to the Indian team. The Bengal fast bowler made the remarks after taking four wickets against Delhi in Bengal's opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season in Kalyani on Sunday. His figures of 4/30 helped Bengal bowl Delhi out for 240 on the first day. Don't detain peaceful protesters, says SC; hundreds still taken away on Day 2. Supreme Court Sunday sought responses of Union home secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi police commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi metro rail chief D Thara to a contempt petition for prima facie violating the court's Oct 9 order against complete shutdown of metro and train services in Delhi on Saturday to thwart CJP's protest seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. 'Virat Kohli was a bit bitter': Ex-India cricketer drops big verdict. Kohli's retirement came after months of uncertainty over his future in Test cricket. Washington golf course could lose up to 529 trees as lawsuit challenges redesign. The National Park Service has proposed the removal of 529 trees at East Potomac Golf Links as part of their maintenance strategy, sparking legal disputes. Park proponents are worried about how this redevelopment might affect local recreation. Concerns also revolve around preserving the historic landscape and transparency about future developments. Despite these discussions, the golf course remains operational while plans evolve. Texas family ends 8-year fight over 65,000-acre ranch worth at least $60m. After years of contention, the heirs of the historic Brite Ranch have finally reached an agreement to split the vast 65,000-acre estate. This ranch, steeped in family history, has faced scrutiny from a court case launched in 2018 that revealed turmoil over trust management and financial allocation. Though lingering issues persist, this resolution is a significant step toward preserving the ranch and averting its sale. US judge blocks Trump's $20 million taxpayer-funded ad campaign. A US court on Sunday ordered the Donald Trump administration to cancel television commercials funded with millions of dollars in taxpayer money to promote the president's political message. Jason Mraz turned old San Diego avocado grove into 17-acre regenerative farm. In 2004, Jason Mraz purchased an avocado grove near San Diego, which he transformed into Mraz Family Farms. Now known for its organic avocados, California-crafted coffee, and seasonal crops, the farm emphasizes regenerative agriculture for enhanced soil health and resilience. Products are supplied to local eateries and shops, and available online, adhering to seasonal availability. This journey showcases Mraz's dedication to sustainability and family-oriented farming.
